open_points.subject: MCP `read_spooled_file` check sequence and implementation path
open_points.text: Conventions: "surface checks it from runs.read_run before read_spooled_file, refusing it with refused"; `read_spooled_file`: "Checks run in that order ... the actor, then the record's existence, then whether its run holds its spool."
open_points.question: Which check order is normative for `read_spooled_file`, and by which operation should `surface` verify SpooledFile existence before deciding `refused` for a run that no longer holds its spool?
options: Check run spool-hold first via `runs.read_run`, then read bytes (existence/bytes checked second).
Check SpooledFile existence first, then spool-hold, then read bytes.
Add/use a metadata-existence read for SpooledFile, then apply the stated order actor -> existence -> spool-hold -> bytes.
open_points.default_guess: Check spool-hold first via `runs.read_run` to preserve the required `refused` outcome when spool is gone, then call `store.read_value_bytes`.

open_points.subject: Effect approval preview file fields vs `read_spooled_file` addressability
open_points.text: A10 rule 2 preview includes, for each file input, "its digest, size and media type"; State 5 says "Wherever an answer shows a spooled file it carries the SpooledFile's full identity, so that the owner can pass it to read_spooled_file".
open_points.question: For approval previews, must file inputs include full SpooledFile identity fields (`run_id`, `producer_node_id`, `map_index`, `attempt_number`, `producer_port`, `list_index`) or only digest/size/media_type?
options: Preview includes full SpooledFile identity (plus digest/size/media_type).
Preview shape depends on caller (owner gets identity, agent may be masked).
open_points.default_guess: Owner preview includes full SpooledFile identity; agent view remains masked per A07.

open_points.subject: `get_repair_view` continuation-token scope on subsequent calls
open_points.text: `get_repair_view` uses "a continuation token that also carries the implementation set of its first page; passed back, it pages only the NodeExecutions below that position for that set ... and every other part is read again as of that request".
open_points.question: What must happen if a caller reuses a `get_repair_view` continuation token with changed request context (different slot, different page size, or other differing paging arguments)?
options: Token is bound to slot and paging context; mismatches are `invalid_request`.
Token is bound only to the embedded implementation set/position; page size may vary.
Token mismatch is tolerated by ignoring conflicting request fields and using token-carried context.
open_points.default_guess: Bind token to slot and token-carried implementation set; allow page-size change but refuse slot/context mismatch as `invalid_request`.
